paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a news report to your campus newspaper on a visit to a local farm organized by your Student Union. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words. ____________________________________________________________________________________________ ____________________________________________________________________________________________ ____________________________________________________________________________________________ PartⅡ Listening Comprehension (25 minutes)

Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and then questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A）, B), C) and D).Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明： 在本节中，您将听到三则新闻报道。在每篇新闻报道的最后，你都会听到两到三个问题。新闻报道和提问均只发言一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A）、B）、C）和 D）的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题1和2是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题3和4是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题5至7是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A），B），C)and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once．
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: The center of American automobile innovation has in the past decade moved 2,000 miles away. It has 26 from Detroit to Silicon Valley, where self-driving vehicles are coming into life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去十年中，美国汽车创新中心已移至 2,000 英里之外。它已经从底特律迁移到硅谷，那里的自动驾驶汽车正在进入人们的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a 27 to take production back to Detroit, Michigan lawmakers have introduced 28 that could make their state the best place in the country, if not the world, to develop self-driving vehicles and put them on the road.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了将生产带回底特律，密歇根州立法者提出了立法，使该州成为美国乃至世界上开发自动驾驶汽车并将其上路的最佳地点。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Michigan’s 29 in auto research and development is under attack from several states and countries which desire to 30 our leadership in transportation. We can’t let happen,” says Senator Mike Kowall, the lead 31 of four bills recently introduced.
paragraphs.translationZh: “密歇根州在汽车研发方面的主导地位正受到多个州和国家的攻击，这些州和国家希望取代我们在交通领域的领导地位。我们不能让这种情况发生，”最近提出的四项法案的主要发起人、参议员迈克·科沃尔 (Mike Kowall) 表示。

paragraphs.sourceText: If all four bills pass as written, they would 32 a substantial update of Michigan’s 2013 law that allowed the testing of self-driving vehicles in limited conditions. Manufacturer would have nearly total freedom to test their self-driving technology on public roads. They would be allowed to send groups of self-driving cars on cross-state road trips, and even set on-demand 33 of self-driving cars, like the one General Motors and Lyft are building.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果所有四项法案都按规定通过，它们将代表密歇根州 2013 年法律的重大更新，该法律允许在有限的条件下测试自动驾驶汽车。制造商几乎可以完全自由地在公共道路上测试他们的自动驾驶技术。他们将被允许派遣一批自动驾驶汽车进行跨州公路旅行，甚至可以按需组建自动驾驶汽车车队，就像通用汽车和 Lyft 正在建造的车队一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: Lawmakers in Michigan clearly want to make the state ready for the commercial application of self-driving technology. In 34 , California, home of Silicon Valley, recently proposed far more 35 rules that would require human drivers be ready to take the wheel, and commercial use of self-driving technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: 密歇根州的立法者显然希望让该州为自动驾驶技术的商业应用做好准备。相比之下，硅谷所在地加利福尼亚州最近提出了更为严格的规则，要求人类驾驶员准备好驾驶，以及自动驾驶技术的商业使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: How Work Will Change When Most of Us Live to 100
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们大多数人活到 100 岁时，工作将会发生怎样的变化

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Today in the United States there are 72,000 centenarians（百岁老人）.Worldwide, Probably 450,000. If current trends continue, then by 2050 there will be more than a million in the US alone. According to the work of Professor James Vaupel and his co-researchers, 50% of babies born in the US in 2007 have a life expectancy of 104 or more. Broadly the same holds for the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Canada, and for Japan 50% of 2007 babies can expect to live to 107.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 今天在美国有 72,000 名百岁老人。全世界大概有 450,000 名。如果目前的趋势继续下去，那么到 2050 年，仅美国就有超过 100 万。根据 James Vaupel 教授及其合作研究人员的研究，2007 年在美国出生的婴儿中有 50% 的预期寿命为 104 岁或以上。英国、德国、法国、意大利和加拿大的情况大致相同，而日本 2007 年的婴儿中有 50% 的预期寿命为 107 岁。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Understandably, there are concerns about what this means for public finances given the associated health and pension challenges. These challenges are real, and society urgently needs to address them. But it is also important to look at the wider picture of what happens when so many people live for 100 years. It is a mistake to simply equate longevity (长寿) with issues of old age. Longer lives have implications for all of life, not just the end of it.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 可以理解的是，考虑到相关的健康和养老金挑战，人们担心这对公共财政意味着什么。这些挑战是真实存在的，社会迫切需要应对这些挑战。但同样重要的是，要从更广泛的角度来看待当这么多人活到 100 岁时会发生什么。简单地将长寿与老年问题等同起来是错误的。更长的寿命对整个生命都有影响，而不仅仅是生命的终结。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Our view is that if many people are living for longer, and are healthier for longer, then this will result in an inevitable redesign of work and life. When people live longer, they are not only older for longer, but also younger for longer. There is some truth in the saying that “70 is the new 60” or “40 the new 30.” If you age more slowly over a longer time period, then you are in some sense younger for longer.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 我们的观点是，如果许多人的寿命更长，健康状况也更长，那么这将不可避免地导致工作和生活的重新设计。当人们寿命更长时，他们不仅年老的时间更长，而且年轻的时间也更长。 “70 岁是新 60 岁”或“40 岁是新 30 岁”这句话有一定道理。如果你在更长的时间内衰老得更慢，那么从某种意义上说，你会更年轻。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) But the changes go further than that. Take, for instance, the age at which people make commitments such as buying a house, getting married, having children, or starting a career. These are all fundamental commitments that are now occurring later in life. In 1962, 50% of Americans were married by age 21. By 2014, that milestone(里程碑)had shifted to age 29.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 但变化远不止于此。以人们做出买房、结婚、生子或开始职业等承诺的年龄为例。这些都是现在在以后的生活中发生的基本承诺。 1962 年，50% 的美国人在 21 岁之前结婚。到 2014 年，这个里程碑已经转移到了 29 岁。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) While there are numerous factors behind these shifts, one factor is surely a growing realization for the young that they are going to live longer. Options are more valuable the longer they can be held. So if you believe you will live longer, then options become more valuable, and early commitment becomes less attractive. The result is that the commitments that previously characterized the beginning of adulthood are now being delayed, and new patterns of behavior and a new stage of life are emerging for those in their twenties.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 虽然这些转变背后有很多因素，但其中一个因素肯定是年轻人越来越意识到他们会活得更长。期权持有时间越长，其价值就越高。因此，如果你相信自己会活得更久，那么选择就会变得更有价值，而早期承诺就会变得不那么有吸引力。结果是，以前作为成年期开始特征的承诺现在被推迟了，对于二十几岁的人来说，新的行为模式和新的生活阶段正在出现。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Longevity also pushes back the age of retirement, and not only for financial reasons. Yes, unless people are prepared to save a lot more, our calculations suggest that if you are now in your mid-40s, then you are likely to work until your early 70s; and if you are in your early 20s, there is a real chance you will need to work until your late 70s or possibly even into your 80s. But even if people are able to economically support a retirement at 65, over thirty years of potential inactivity is harmful to cognitive(认知的) and emotional vitality. Many people may simply not want to do it.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 长寿也会推迟退休年龄，这不仅仅是出于经济原因。是的，除非人们准备好存更多钱，否则我们的计算表明，如果您现在 40 多岁，那么您很可能会工作到 70 岁出头；如果你才 20 多岁，那么你很有可能需要工作到 70 多岁，甚至可能到 80 多岁。但即使人们能够在经济上支持 65 岁的退休生活，超过 30 年的潜在不活动也会损害认知和情感活力。许多人可能根本不想这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) And yet that does not mean that simply extending our careers is appealing. Just lengthening that second stage of full-time work may secure the financial assets needed for a 100-year life, but such persistent work will inevitably exhaust precious intangible assets such as productive skills, vitality, happiness, and friendship.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 然而，这并不意味着简单地延长我们的职业生涯就很有吸引力。仅仅延长第二阶段的全职工作或许可以保证100岁生活所需的金融资产，但这种持续的工作将不可避免地耗尽生产技能、活力、幸福和友谊等宝贵的无形资产。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) The same is true for education. It is impossible that a single shot of education, administered in childhood and early adulthood, will be able to support a sustained, 60-year career. If you factor in the projected rates of technological change, either your skills will become unnecessary, or your industry outdated. That means that everyone will, at some point in their life, have to make a number of major reinvestments in their skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 教育也是如此。在儿童期和成年早期进行的一次教育不可能支持持续 60 年的职业生涯。如果你考虑到技术变革的预计速度，要么你的技能将变得不必要，要么你的行业就会过时。这意味着每个人在一生中的某个时刻都必须对自己的技能进行一些重大的再投资。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) It seems likely, then, that the traditional three-stage life will evolve into multiple stages containing two, three, or oven more different careers. Each of these stages could potentially be different. In one the focus could be on building financial success and personal achievement, in another on creating a better work/life balance, still another on exploring and understanding options more fully, or becoming an independent producer, yet another on making a social contribution. These stages will span sectors, take people to different cities, and provide foundation for building a wide variety of skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）那么，传统的三阶段人生很可能会演变成包含两个、三个或更多不同职业的多个阶段。每个阶段都可能有所不同。其中一个重点可能是建立财务成功和个人成就，另一个重点是创造更好的工作/生活平衡，还有一个重点是更充分地探索和理解选择，或者成为一名独立制片人，还有一个重点是做出社会贡献。这些阶段将跨越各个部门，将人们带到不同的城市，并为培养各种技能提供基础。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Transitions between stages could be marked with sabbaticals (休假) as people find time to rest and recharge their health, re-invest in their relationships, or improve their skills. At times, these breaks and transitions will be self-determined, at others they will be forced as existing roles, firms, or industries cease to exist. K ）A multi-stage life will have profound changes not just in how you manage your career, but also in your approach to life. An increasingly important skill will be your ability to deal with change and even welcome it. A three-stage life has few transitions, while a multi-stage life has many. That is why being self-aware, investing in broader networks of friends, and being open to new ideas will become even more crucial skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 阶段之间的过渡可以用休假来标记，因为人们有时间休息和恢复健康、重新投资于他们的人际关系或提高他们的技能。有时，这些突破和转变是自我决定的，而有时，它们是由于现有角色、公司或行业不复存在而被迫的。 K）多阶段的人生不仅会在你的职业生涯管理方式上发生深刻的变化，还会在你的生活方式上发生深刻的变化。一项日益重要的技能将是你应对变化甚至欢迎变化的能力。三阶段人生的转变很少，而多阶段人生则有很多转变。这就是为什么自我意识、投资于更广泛的朋友网络以及对新想法持开放态度将成为更加重要的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) These multi-stage lives will create extraordinary variety across groups of people simply because there are so many ways of sequencing the stages. More stages mean more possible sequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这些多阶段的生活将在人群中创造出非凡的多样性，因为有很多不同的方式来对各个阶段进行排序。更多阶段意味着更多可能的序列。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) With this variety will come the end of the close association of age and stage. I n a three-stage life, people leave university at the same time and the same age, they tend to start their careers and family at the same age, they proceed through middle management all roughly the same time, and then move into retirement within a few years of each other. In a multi-stage life, you could be an undergraduate at 20, 40, or 60; a manager at 30, 50, or 70; and become an independent producer at any age.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 随着这种变化，年龄和阶段的紧密联系将会结束。在三阶段人生中，人们在同一时间和同一年龄离开大学，他们往往在同一年龄开始自己的职业生涯和家庭，他们大致在同一时间进入中层管理，然后在彼此相隔几年内退休。在多阶段的人生中，你可能在 20 岁、40 岁或 60 岁时成为一名大学生； 30、50 或 70 岁的经理；并在任何年龄成为独立制片人。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Current life structures, career paths, educational choices, and social norms are out of tune with the emerging reality of longer lifespans. The three-stage life of full-time education, followed by continuous work, and then complete retirement may have worked for our parents or even grandparents, but it is not relevant today. We believe that to focus on longevity as primarily an issue of aging is to miss its full implications. Longevity is not necessarily about being older for longer. It is about living longer, being older later, and being younger longer.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 当前的生活结构、职业道路、教育选择和社会规范与寿命延长的现实格格不入。全日制教育、持续工作、然后完全退休的三阶段生活可能对我们的父母甚至祖父母来说很有效，但在今天已经不适用了。我们认为，将长寿主要视为衰老问题就会忽视其全部含义。长寿并不一定意味着年龄更长。它是关于活得更长、晚一点、年轻一点的时间更长。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. An extended lifespan in the future will allow people to have more careers than now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 未来寿命的延长将使人们拥有比现在更多的职业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Just extending one’s career may have both positive and negative effects.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37.仅仅延长一个人的职业生涯可能会产生积极和消极的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Nowadays, many Americans have on average delayed their marriage by some eight years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 如今，许多美国人的婚姻平均推迟了八年左右。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Because of their longer lifespan, young people today no longer follow the pattern of life of their parents or grandparents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 由于寿命更长，今天的年轻人不再遵循父母或祖父母的生活模式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Many more people will be expected to live over 100 by the mid-21st century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 到 21 世纪中叶，预计将有更多的人活到 100 岁以上。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. A longer life will cause radical changes in people’s approach to life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 寿命的延长将导致人们的生活方式发生根本性的变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Fast technological change makes it necessary for one to constantly upgrade their skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 快速的技术变革使得人们有必要不断提升自己的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Many people may not want to retire early because it would do harm to their mental and emotional well-being.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 许多人可能不想提前退休，因为这会损害他们的精神和情感健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The close link between age and stage may cease to exist in a multi-stage life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 在多阶段的生活中，年龄和阶段之间的密切联系可能不再存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. People living a longer and healthier life will have to rearrange their work and life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 人们要活得更长寿、更健康，就必须重新安排他们的工作和生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the classic marriage vow（誓约）, couples promise to stay together in sickness and in health. But a new study finds that the risk of divorce among older couples rises when the wife-not the husband—becomes seriously ill.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在经典的婚姻誓约中，夫妻承诺无论疾病还是健康都将在一起。但一项新的研究发现，当妻子（而不是丈夫）病重时，老年夫妇离婚的风险就会上升。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Married women diagnosed with a serious health condition may find themselves struggling with the impact of their disease while also experiencing the stress of divorce,” said researcher Amelia Karraker.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员阿米莉亚·卡拉克（Amelia Karraker）表示：“被诊断出患有严重健康问题的已婚女性可能会发现自己在与疾病的影响作斗争，同时也承受着离婚的压力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Karraker and co-author Kenzie Latham analyzed 20 years of data on 2,717 marriages from a study conducted by Indiana University since 1992. At the time of the first interview, at least one of the partners was over the age of
paragraphs.translationZh: Karraker 和合著者 Kenzie Latham 分析了印第安纳大学自 1992 年以来进行的一项研究中 2,717 起婚姻的 20 年数据。在第一次采访时，至少有一个伴侣的年龄超过

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers examined how the onset（发生）of four serious physical illnesses affected marriages. They found that, overall, 31% of marriages ended in divorce over the period studied. The incidence of new chronic（慢性的）illness onset increased over time as will, with more husbands than wives developing serious health problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员研究了四种严重身体疾病的发作如何影响婚姻。他们发现，总体而言，在研究期间，31% 的婚姻以离婚告终。新的慢性疾病发病率随着时间的推移而增加，出现严重健康问题的丈夫多于妻子。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We found that women are doubly vulnerable to marital break-up in the face of illness,” Karraker said. “They’re more likely to be widowed, and if they’re the noes who become ill, they’re more likely to get divorced.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 卡拉克说：“我们发现，女性在面对疾病时更容易陷入婚姻破裂。” “他们更有可能成为寡妇，如果他们是生病的人，他们更有可能离婚。”

paragraphs.sourceText: While the study didn’t assess why divorce in more likely when wives but not husbands become seriously ill, Karraker offers a few possible reasons. “Gender norms and social expectations about caregiving many make it more difficult for men to provide care to sick spouses,” Karraker said. “And because of the imbalance in marriage markets, especially in older ages, divorced men have more choices among prospective partners than divorced women.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然该研究没有评估为什么当妻子而不是丈夫患重病时离婚的可能性更大，但卡拉克提供了一些可能的原因。卡拉克说：“性别规范和社会对护理的期望使男性更难为生病的配偶提供护理。” “而且由于婚姻市场的不平衡，尤其是年龄较大的人，离婚男性比离婚女性在未来伴侣方面有更多选择。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Given the increasing concern about health care costs for the aging population, Karraker believes policymakers should be aware of the relationship between disease and risk of divorce.
paragraphs.translationZh: 鉴于人们日益关注老龄化人口的医疗保健费用，卡拉克认为政策制定者应该意识到疾病与离婚风险之间的关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Offering support services to spouses caring for their other halves may reduce marital stress and prevent divorce at older ages,” she said. “But it’s also important to recognize that the pressure to divorce may be health-related and that sick ex-wives may need additional care and services to prevent worsening health and increased health costs.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “为照顾另一半的配偶提供支持服务可能会减轻婚姻压力并防止老年离婚，”她说。 “但同样重要的是要认识到离婚的压力可能与健康有关，生病的前妻可能需要额外的护理和服务，以防止健康状况恶化和医疗费用增加。”

paragraphs.sourceText: If you were like most children, you probably got upset when your mother called you by a sibling’s(兄弟姐妹的)name. How could she not know you? Did it mean she loved you less?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你像大多数孩子一样，当你的母亲用兄弟姐妹的名字称呼你时，你可能会感到不安。她怎么会不认识你呢？这是否意味着她对你的爱减少了？

paragraphs.sourceText: Probably not. According to the first research to tackle this topic head-on, misnaming the most familiar people in our life is a common cognitive (认知的)error that has to do with how our memories classify and store familiar names.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可能不会。根据第一项正面解决这个话题的研究，给我们生活中最熟悉的人起错误的名字是一种常见的认知错误，这与我们的记忆如何分类和存储熟悉的名字有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study, published online in April in the journal Memory and Cognition,found that the “wrong” name is not random but is invariably fished out from the same relationship pond: children, siblings, friends. The study did not examine the possibility of deep psychological significance to the mistake, says psychologist David Rubin, “but it does tell us who’s in and who’s out of the group.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究于四月在线发表在《记忆与认知》杂志上，发现“错误”的名字不是随机的，而是总是从同一个关系池中捞出来：孩子、兄弟姐妹、朋友。心理学家大卫·鲁宾（David Rubin）表示，这项研究并没有考察这个错误是否具有深刻的心理意义，“但它确实告诉我们谁在这个群体中，谁在这个群体之外。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The study also found that within that group, misnamings occurred where the names shared initial or internal sounds, like Jimmy and Joanie or John and Bob. Physical resemblance between people was not a factor. Nor was gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究还发现，在该群体中，如果名字的首字母或内部发音相同，就会出现错误命名，例如吉米和乔安妮或约翰和鲍勃。人与人之间的外貌相似性并不是一个因素。性别也不是。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers conducted five separate surveys of more than 1,700 people. Some of the surveys included only college students; others were done with a mixed-age population. Some asked subjects about incidents where someone close to them—family or friend—had called them by another person’s name. The other surveys asked about times when subjects had themselves called someone close to them by the wrong name. All the surveys found that people mixed up names within relationship groups such as grandchildren, friends and siblings but hardly ever crossed these boundaries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员对 1,700 多人进行了五次单独的调查。有些调查只包括大学生；有些则只包括大学生。另一些则针对不同年龄的人群。一些人询问受试者一些与他们关系密切的人（家人或朋友）用另一个人的名字称呼他们的事件。其他调查询问了受试者自己叫错亲近的人的次数。所有调查都发现，人们在孙子、朋友和兄弟姐妹等关系群体中混淆了名字，但很少跨越这些界限。

paragraphs.sourceText: In general, the study found that undergraduates were almost as likely as old people to make this mistake and men as likely as women. Older people and this mistake and men as likely as women. Older people and women made the mistake slightly more often, but that may be because grandparents have more grandchildren to mix up than parents have children. Also, mothers may call on their children more often than fathers, given traditional gender norms. There was no evidence that errors occurred more when the misnamer was frustrated, tired or angry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总的来说，研究发现，大学生犯这种错误的可能性几乎与老年人一样，男性和女性也一样。老年人出现这种错误的可能性与男性和女性一样。老年人和女性犯这种错误的频率稍高一些，但这可能是因为祖父母有更多的孙子孙女，而不是父母的孩子。此外，考虑到传统的性别规范，母亲可能比父亲更频繁地拜访孩子。没有证据表明当错误命名者感到沮丧、疲倦或愤怒时，错误发生得更多。
